rust_summary: a mod's promise that it stays out of the mobs' turns, so a level's mobs may tick in groups on several threads (`native_mob_phase_quiet`).
doc_summary: `native_mob_phase_quiet(quiet)` (server): with `HORIZON_PARALLEL_TICK` on, the server ticks a level's mobs in groups on several threads only while every loaded mod sets `*quiet = true` here, each asked on its own once a tick. Set it only when the mod hooks none of what runs in a mob's turn: `native_living_change_target`, `native_living_heal`, `native_living_breathe`, `native_living_drown`, `native_living_fall`, `native_living_death_message`, `native_register_goals` (its goals run in the turns), `native_living_incoming_damage` (all versions), `native_living_damage_pre`, `native_living_knockback`, a content mod effect's ticks, and no mixin into those. `native_living_jump` and `native_living_damage_post` may stay hooked: in a grouped tick they are told on the server thread after the mobs ticked, in their order. A mod that doesn't set it keeps the mobs on the server thread, as before. Bundles that use it need "hooks": @API:mob_phase_quiet@.
